headline: Sensex and Nifty face volatility amid FII outflows and oil concerns, marking worst monthly performance since March.

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Persistent FII outflows and selling pressure are weighing on the benchmark indices
Fluctuating global crude oil prices have sparked concerns and capital outflows
Global interest rate hike bets are impacting investor sentiment in domestic markets
Benchmark indices failed to maintain intraday gains amidst high market volatility
whatHappening: The Indian rupee rebounded to 95.83 against the US dollar as crude prices eased
Sensex and Nifty extended their losing streak to a third consecutive session
Indian benchmark indices are set to post their worst nine-month show in 15 years
The Nifty 50 recently managed to end above the 22,700 mark despite a 50-point drop in Sensex
summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty recorded their worst monthly performance since March due to persistent FII outflows and high crude oil prices. Although the Indian Rupee recovered slightly to 95.83 against the dollar, the market remains volatile and has struggled to sustain intraday gains. Investors are cautious as global rate hike concerns and capital outflows contribute to the market's worst nine-month performance in 15 years.
